div.head: I Cn 2
div.ab: And [uton] Godes cyrican griðian ⁊ friðian ⁊ gelomlice secean saulum to hæle ⁊ us sylfum to þearfe.
And witan Godes cyrican griþian ⁊ friþian ⁊ gelomlice seacean us sylfum to þearfe.
And uton Godes cirican griðian ⁊ friðian ⁊ gelomlice secan us silfan to þearfe.
Et sanctam Dei ęcclesiam pacificare, custodire, frequentare ad nostram semper utilitatem satagamus (gaudeamus).
And [uton] Godes cyrican griðian ⁊ friðian ⁊ gelomlice secean saulum to hæle ⁊ us sylfum to þearfe.
And let us maintain the security and sanctity of the churches of God and frequently attend them for the salvation of our souls and our own benefit.
und lasst uns Gottes Kirchen mit Schutzgewalt und Friedensrecht umgeben und häufig besuchen den Seelen zum Heile und uns selbst zu Nutze.
and let us protect and keep the peace of God's churches and visit them often, for the salvation of souls and for our own benefit.
div.note: ‘uton’ is supplied in G from D and A (Liebermann). ‘saulum to hæle ⁊’ is probably G's interpolation. In D, II Cn 1–7 follows 2.2, then I Cn 6. Liebermann compares VI Atr 42.3.
